props.name: children
props.description: The row's content. Direct `SelectionItem.SubSection` children render outside the label, so a field or button in one never toggles the control, and everything else renders in the label row. The row finds a direct SubSection whether a server or a client component wrote it. In a client component, a Fragment, another component or an HOC around a SubSection hides it, and it stays inside the label. Pass such a band through `subSections`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes for the row, merged last. A `px-*` utility sets the card's side inset, and a click in that inset beside the label row toggles the control. The row paints the card fill (`bg-card`) like the other field boxes. A list on a surface that should show through takes a background class such as `bg-background`, which replaces it. The row states its fill as `--surface`, the colour a chart's cut-outs paint, so a row that paints another opaque fill restates `--surface` and `--surface-muted-foreground` beside it, such as `className="bg-background [--surface:var(--background)] [--surface-muted-foreground:var(--muted-foreground)]"`. The checked row's `bg-muted` tint and the disabled row's `--selection-disabled-background` fill win over such a class. Set `--selection-disabled-background`, for example to `var(--background)`, to change the disabled fill. The edges and the lines between rows come from the `--selection-*` theme roles, which the Tokens section lists. Stacked rows share one line per join, and a horizontal group's rows are cards of their own with no line between them. Set a role on the element that carries the theme attributes, `<html>` or a `ThemeScope`. For example, `--selection-border: var(--border)` on the `ThemeScope` gives branded rows an outer edge. On a plain wrapper the rows keep the edges the theme element resolved. A checked row below another draws its top edge by pulling itself up 1px, so a margin class on the row can break that edge.

props.name: control
props.description: The control the row selects, such as a `Checkbox`, a `RadioGroupItem` or a `Switch`, in the row's icon slot. `CheckboxItem` and `RadioItem` take no icon. To show one beside the control, pass the control and the icon together here, and hide the icon with `aria-hidden` so the row's title and description stay the control's name.

props.name: controlPosition
props.description: Where the control sits in the row: before the content, or after it at `end`.

props.name: dataSlot
props.description: The `data-slot` the row's `Field.Item` root carries, such as `"checkbox-item"` or `"radio-item"`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the wrapped control should ignore user interaction. The `disabled` prop on `<Field.Root>` takes precedence over this.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Shows the disabled row: the `not-allowed` cursor and the theme's `--selection-disabled-background` fill under a 45° hatch striped in `--selection-disabled-hatch`. Neutral themes fill with `--muted` under black stripes at 2% alpha, and branded themes keep the card fill with no stripes. The row's text, its SubSection's included, takes `--selection-disabled-foreground`, which is the foreground in neutral themes and the muted foreground in branded ones. A text colour class in `className` still wins, a description keeps its own muted text, and the control dims itself. A row shows the same look without this prop when its group is disabled, or when its control carries `data-disabled`, matches `:disabled` or is `aria-disabled="true"`. It does not disable the control. Disable the control or the group for that.

props.name: isSubSectionSelectable
props.description: Lets a click on a SubSection's passive parts toggle the control: its text, the band around it and the side padding beside it. A click inside a link, button, form field, label or other focusable element in the SubSection stays that element's, and a click that ends a text selection does nothing. The control's accessible name stays the label row, and keyboard and assistive-technology users toggle through the control. Leave it off when the SubSection reveals fields under the control, so a click between those fields does not clear the choice.

props.name: render
props.type: ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, FieldItemState> | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | undefined
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: subSections
props.description: Band content passed apart from the row children, rendered outside the label before any direct `SelectionItem.SubSection` children. A SubSection inside a wrapper the partition cannot see through goes here. Direct SubSection children need no help: the shell recognises them whether a server or a client component wrote them.

props.name: children
props.description: The footer's content, wrapped in an inner `item-footer-content` element. A `hidden` or `visible` footer clips content that reaches more than 0.25rem past that element's box. That includes absolutely positioned content with no positioned ancestor inside the footer, which positions against the inner element. Keep 0.25rem of inset on a zero-inset item flush against a scroll container's edge, or that room scrolls. A `default` footer never clips.

props.name: mode
props.description: Whether the footer shows. `hidden` collapses its row to zero height, clips it and makes it inert. Switching between `hidden` and `visible` animates the height with a fade and a short slide, so content below moves instead of jumping. Switching to `default` snaps.
